headline: COPPER CRASHES TO 4-MONTH LOW: LME Drops to $13,550/Tonne as AI Demand Correlation Breaks With Tech Selloff
snippet: Benchmark copper on the London Metal Exchange fell 1.9% to US$13,550 per tonne on November 13 — its lowest since July 20 — as sticky U.S. inflation data lifted rate-hike expectations and weak AI-linked tech stocks weighed on demand sentiment. Analysts flagged copper's growing correlation with AI-sector performance as a new structural risk: when AI data-centre build-out hopes fade, copper demand projections deflate with them, compounding pressure from the broader macro tightening trade.

headline: GOLD MINERS SNAP BACK THURSDAY: GDX and Producers Rally as Bullion Claws Above $3,900 After CPI Rout
snippet: Gold mining stocks advanced Thursday as bullion recovered from Wednesday's inflation-driven slide, tracking a rebound in spot gold back above $3,900. The recovery is being treated cautiously by analysts who note December Fed rate-hike pricing has not fully reversed — Newmont is trading near its 200-day moving average and institutional flows remain ambiguous — but the bounce is halting a string of back-to-back down sessions for the GDX and GDXJ.

headline: NORDIQUE CRITICAL METALS: 95%+ Rare Earth Leaching Efficiency at Kwyjibo — Smaller 10,000t/yr Processing Plant Unlocked
snippet: Nordique Critical Metals (TSXV: NQC) announced November 13 that laboratory hydrometallurgical tests on Kwyjibo rare earth samples achieved leaching efficiencies exceeding 95% for neodymium, dysprosium and yttrium — the three most critical magnet metals. The result supports a redesigned, smaller processing plant targeting more than 10,000 tonnes of rare earth oxides annually, reducing capital intensity and improving the project's path to financing at a time when non-Chinese RE processing capacity commands a premium from Western governments and industrial buyers.

headline: METALS COMPANY Q3: Korea Zinc Capital, Allseas Nodule Pact, NOAA Compliance — Deep-Sea Mining Timeline Advances
snippet: The Metals Company (Nasdaq: TMC) provided its Q3 2026 corporate update following a November 12 conference call, highlighting three milestones that advance its polymetallic nodule programme: Korea Zinc's $85 million equity injection, a signed commercial agreement with Allseas for the first offshore nodule recovery operation, and NOAA's finding of Substantial Compliance for TMC USA's consolidated ISA application. Together these move the world's first deep-sea critical mineral harvest from regulatory concept toward operational reality, with Clarion-Clipperton Zone nodules carrying cobalt, nickel, copper and manganese.

headline: CHINA SCRAMBLES FOR COPPER: Shanghai Inventories Crash 24% in One Week to Three-Year Low as DRC Crackdown Bites
snippet: Shanghai-monitored copper warehouse inventories fell more than 24% in a single week to their lowest level in nearly three years as Chinese buyers scrambled for physical metal amid a crackdown on illegal copper mining in the Democratic Republic of Congo — which supplies roughly 10% of global mined copper. The acute tightness in China's domestic market is running directly counter to the LME price selloff, creating a significant basis divergence and a potential floor under any further Western futures-driven decline.

headline: SUN SUMMIT MINERALS: 12km Porphyry Corridor Mapped at Buck Project BC — IP Anomaly Expanded for Winter Drilling
snippet: Sun Summit Minerals (TSXV: SMN) announced November 12 that its summer 2026 programme at the Buck Project in central British Columbia identified a 12.0 km trend of porphyry targets and expanded the CR South IP chargeability anomaly — a key drill-target indicator for porphyry-style copper-gold mineralisation. The company plans DCIP geophysical surveys and soil geochemical work over the largely drift-covered CR Porphyry Trend to refine drill targets ahead of a planned winter programme, adding to what is shaping up as a district-scale exploration story in BC's productive porphyry belt.

headline: STORM EXPLORATION HITS SULPHIDE MINERALIZATION IN ALL 8 HOLES AT GOLD STANDARD ONTARIO — Assays Q1 2027
snippet: Storm Exploration (TSXV: STRM) reported November 12 that all eight recently drilled holes at its Gold Standard Project in Ontario intersected sulphide mineralization — a 100% hit rate that confirms the structural target is regionally consistent across the entire programme footprint. Laboratory assays are due in Q1 2027, and the company notes that visible sulphides in all holes provides strong geological confidence in advance of the numbers, underpinning the rationale for a follow-up programme.

headline: ZACKS: 4 GOLD MINERS POSITIONED TO OUTLAST THE HEADWINDS — Newmont, B2Gold, Fury Gold, Gold Royalty Make the Cut
snippet: Zacks Investment Research identified four gold mining names with the balance sheet strength and earnings trajectory to weather the November 2026 sector selloff: Newmont (NEM), B2Gold (BTO), Fury Gold Mines, and Gold Royalty Corp. The analysis notes NEM's Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 earnings has risen 1.4% over the past 30 days, implying 33.2% year-over-year EPS growth even as the stock corrects — a classic setup where institutional analysts are upgrading through price weakness, which historically precedes sector recovery.

headline: MORNING BRIEFING: Gold AND Copper Both Hit Multi-Month Lows — Rare Double-Selloff Points to Macro Stress, Not Metal-Specific Weakness
snippet: Mining Stock Daily's November 13 morning briefing flags a rare and significant market condition: gold and copper hitting multi-month lows simultaneously, suggesting the current sell-off is macro-driven — rooted in U.S. rate-hike repricing — rather than a commodity-specific story. When both metals fall together, it historically signals institutional de-risking across all commodity exposures simultaneously, which typically produces the deepest near-term drawdowns but also sets up the sharpest recoveries once the macro trigger resolves.

headline: SILVER FALLS TO $50.91 AS GOLD-SILVER RATIO WIDENS TO 77.22 — FXStreet Tracks Nov 12 CPI-Driven Precious Metals Rout
snippet: Silver fell 1.6% to $50.91 per ounce on November 12 as the hot U.S. CPI print drove up December Fed rate-hike expectations, with the gold-silver ratio widening to 77.22. FXStreet notes that silver has fallen roughly 28% from its 2026 year-to-date highs — a steeper correction than gold's — which precious metals strategists attribute to silver's industrial demand component making it more sensitive to growth fears layered on top of the same monetary tightening headwinds weighing on gold.
